subject: Critical Thinking
title: Groupthink: When Agreement Becomes Dangerous
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Groupthink: When Agreement Becomes Dangerous.

hook.text: JFK's advisors were brilliant individually. Together, they approved the Bay of Pigs invasion. Nobody dissented.

buildup.text: Groupthink: a group's desire for harmony overrides realistic evaluation of alternatives.

discovery.text: Irving Janis identified it in 1972: self-censorship, illusion of unanimity, pressure on dissenters, & stereotyping.

twist.text: The Challenger disaster, Enron's collapse, and the Iraq WMD intelligence failure — all classic groupthink.

climax.text: The fix: assign a devil's advocate, encourage dissent, and have the leader speak last to avoid anchoring.

punchline.text: If everyone agrees, someone isn't thinking.

quiz.question: What causes groupthink?
options: The desire for group harmony overrides critical evaluation

details.summary: Groupthink occurs when the desire for harmony in a group overrides realistic evaluation of alternatives. It suppresses dissent, ignores warning signs, and produces catastrophically bad collective decisions.
details.whyItMatters: Groupthink contributed to the Bay of Pigs invasion, the Challenger disaster, and many corporate failures. Understanding it helps you prevent it in your own teams.
takeaways: Groupthink prioritizes consensus over critical evaluation
Symptoms include self-censorship and illusion of unanimity
Appointing a devil's advocate can break the pattern

faq.question: What are the warning signs of groupthink in a team meeting?
faq.answer: Watch for rapid agreement without debate, pressure on dissenters to conform, self-censorship of doubts, and the assumption that silence means agreement. If nobody disagrees, groupthink may be operating.

faq.question: How can a leader prevent groupthink in their organization?
faq.answer: Assign a devil's advocate role, invite outside opinions, withhold your own view until others have spoken, and explicitly reward dissent. Creating psychological safety for disagreement is essential.
